children: on Thursday introduced three high-end Walkman digital music players priced at up to $5,899, featuring upgraded audio circuitry, larger displays and software enhancements aimed at audiophiles.
The lineup comprises the NW-WM1ZM3, priced at $5,899; the NW-WM1AM3 at $2,999.99; and the NW-ZX900 at $1,899.99. All three are available for preorder, although shipping dates have not been announced.
The flagship model features a gold-plated oxygen-free copper chassis, while the other two use aluminum-alloy main enclosures and gold-plated copper rear panels. Sony
has also upgraded the power supply components in the WM1-series models to improve power stability and reduce interference.

S-Master HX digital amplifier and an updated DSD Remastering Engine, which converts PCM audio into an 11.2MHz DSD stream. The remastering technology now works with both downloaded and Wi-Fi-streamed music.

The WM1-series devices have 5.5-inch displays, while the ZX900 has a 5-inch screen. All three feature 1080p resolution and run Android software, with the ZX900 moving to Android 16 from Android 12 in its predecessor.
